attribute-control-chart.name: Control Chart (Attribute)
attribute-control-chart.description: SPC charts for count data: p, np, c, u
attribute-control-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart counted data: p and np for defectives, c and u for defects, with Nelson-type rules on the plotted points.

attribute-test.name: Attribute Tests
attribute-test.description: Tests for proportions, rates and counts: 1 and 2 proportions, Fisher's exact, chi-square association, McNemar, equivalence (TOST), 1 and 2 Poisson rates
attribute-test.whenToUse: When counts of events are compared: tests one proportion against a hypothesized value, two proportions against each other (z test and Fisher's exact test), the equivalence of proportions (TOST), paired proportions before and after (McNemar), one or two Poisson rates (events per exposure) or the association of two categorical variables (chi-square on a cross table). The counts are given as summarized numbers or taken from worksheet columns.

bar.name: Bar Chart
bar.description: Bar chart from worksheet columns: frequency, mean, or sum per category
bar.whenToUse: Compare counts or values across categories, optionally split or stacked by a group.

boxplot.name: Boxplot
boxplot.whenToUse: Compare the spread, median and outliers of one or more numeric columns, optionally split by a group.

calculator.name: Calculator
calculator.description: Scientific calculator with statistics and 6σ mode
calculator.whenToUse: When a number, a statistic or a process capability has to be computed quickly without setting up a data collection — scientifically, as a location and spread measure over a short list of values, or as Cp/Cpk, sigma level and DPMO from values and specification limits; not for a lasting analysis over a data table, that is what the data collection, the histogram and the process capability analysis are for.

ce-matrix.name: C&E Matrix
ce-matrix.whenToUse: When several process inputs are to be ranked by how strongly they act on the outputs that matter to the customer — the weighted row sum says which input to investigate first; not for rating failure modes by occurrence and detection, which is what the FMEA is for.

chart-suggestion.name: Chart Suggestion
chart-suggestion.description: Proposes suitable chart types for the selected columns
chart-suggestion.whenToUse: You have columns of a worksheet and need to know which chart fits their roles — a ranked list with a preview, from which the chosen chart opens as a module of its own.

contour-plot.name: Contour Plot
contour-plot.description: Visualize response surfaces z = f(x, y) as contour diagrams
contour-plot.whenToUse: Draw the response surface of a two-factor model as contour lines — from polynomial coefficients or an own formula in x and y — optionally with measured points.

control-chart.name: Control Chart
control-chart.description: SPC control charts for process stability
control-chart.whenToUse: Monitor a process over time with Shewhart limits: I-MR for single values, X̄-R or X̄-S for subgroups, with Nelson rules, stages, annotations and frozen Phase II limits.

correlation.name: Correlation Analysis
correlation.description: Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation between variables
correlation.whenToUse: When two or more numeric variables may be related: computes the correlation of two columns (Pearson, Spearman and Kendall side by side, with confidence interval and diagnostics) or of three or more columns as a correlation matrix; each column needs at least 5 numeric values.

data-import.name: Data Import
data-import.description: Read data from third-party formats (Minitab .mpx, CSV/TSV/TXT, Excel/ODS, JSON/NDJSON, Q-DAS AQDEF) into a worksheet
data-import.whenToUse: When data from a third-party source is to be brought into a data collection; for an agent from CSV or JSON text, with profiles for common measuring-machine exports.

data-transformation.name: Data Transformation
data-transformation.description: Transform data (Box-Cox, Johnson, Log, …) for normality
data-transformation.whenToUse: When non-normal measurements should be transformed for a method that assumes normality — Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson, Johnson, logarithm, square root, reciprocal, square — and the result is reused as a new column. Requires the measurements as a numeric column of a data collection (at least three values).

deployment-flowchart.name: Deployment Flowchart
deployment-flowchart.description: Process chain across role lanes — makes hand-offs visible
deployment-flowchart.whenToUse: When an existing chain needs to show which role owns which step and where the hand-offs are — not for capturing a new process without a role assignment yet.

distribution-fit.name: Distribution Fit
distribution-fit.description: Fit data to multiple distributions and rank by Goodness-of-Fit test
distribution-fit.whenToUse: When it is unclear which distribution describes a measured characteristic: fits normal, lognormal, Weibull, exponential and further distributions to one numeric column and ranks them by goodness of fit; requires at least 5 values.

dmaic-calendar.name: Calendar
dmaic-calendar.description: Project calendar: appointments per phase in a month and a week view
dmaic-calendar.whenToUse: When the appointments of a project should be kept — meetings, measurement windows, deadlines —, each assigned to a phase and shown in a month or week view; not for tasks without a fixed point in time, that is what the todo list is for, and not for planning activity durations and dependencies.

doe-advisor.name: DoE Advisor
doe-advisor.description: Overview of DoE designs and a guided wizard for design selection
doe-advisor.whenToUse: When an improvement project still has to settle WHICH design of experiments fits — screening, interactions, optimisation, robustness or mixture — or when the Overview tab with all designs and the comparison of the central composite designs are needed; not for planning or evaluating a concrete experiment, that is what the design planner and its evaluation are for.

doe-planner.name: DoE Planner
doe-planner.description: Design of Experiments: Full Factorial, Fractional, Plackett-Burman, CCD, Box-Behnken, Taguchi
doe-planner.whenToUse: When the effect of several factors on one or more responses is to be studied in a planned experiment: full or fractional factorial, Plackett-Burman, response surface (CCD, Box-Behnken), Taguchi or optimal (D, A, G), also as an EVOP project over several phases. Which design type fits is settled beforehand in the DoE advisor (doe-advisor).

five-why.name: 5-Why Analysis
five-why.description: Root cause analysis with branching question paths
five-why.whenToUse: When a single concrete incident is to be traced to its root and the domain knowledge is in the room — not for statistical relationships across many cases.

fmea.name: FMEA
fmea.description: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis with RPN calculation
fmea.whenToUse: When a process or a design should be surveyed systematically for what can go wrong, what effect it has, how often it occurs and how reliably it is detected — rated by action priority (AIAG-VDA) or risk priority number, with actions and their effect on the rating; not for collecting possible causes without rating them, that is what Ishikawa and the cause-and-effect matrix are for.

gage-run-chart.name: Gage Run Chart
gage-run-chart.description: Plots every single measurement grouped by part and appraiser against a common reference line — reveals appraiser bias and unusual parts.
gage-run-chart.whenToUse: Look at a measurement system study before computing statistics: every measurement per part and operator, against a reference line.

heatmap.name: Heatmap
heatmap.description: Cross-tabulation as a color-coded grid — cell color shows frequency, mean, or sum per (X, G) combination.
heatmap.whenToUse: Show a value or a count for every combination of two categories as a colour grid — e.g. cycle time per shift and line.

histogram.name: Histogram
histogram.description: Frequency distribution with boxplot and statistics
histogram.whenToUse: Show the distribution of one or more numeric columns as frequency bars, with summary statistics and a confidence interval.

hypothesis-test.name: Hypothesis Test
hypothesis-test.description: Variance and mean tests with automatic normality assessment and power analysis
hypothesis-test.whenToUse: When you need to decide whether an observed difference in location or spread goes beyond the noise — one mean against a target value, two samples against each other, or k groups together. Requires metric data in a data collection.

individual-value-plot.name: Individual Value Plot
individual-value-plot.description: Plot every individual observation per group as a point
individual-value-plot.whenToUse: Show every single value of one or more numeric columns, grouped by up to three categories, with mean and confidence interval per group.

ishikawa.name: Ishikawa 6M
ishikawa.description: Root cause analysis with 6M categories and expert scoring
ishikawa.whenToUse: When possible causes of a problem are to be collected, ordered by 6M and rated by the team, so that the most likely ones get tested with experiments; states can be kept as snapshots and compared. For a single chain of causes by asking why, use 5-Why.

kano.name: Kano Model
kano.description: Classify and prioritize requirements from the VoC→CTx tree using the Kano method
kano.whenToUse: When features should be classified by how much their presence raises satisfaction and their absence lowers it — must-be, performance and delight features, surveyed with the functional and the dysfunctional question per respondent; not for weighting criteria against each other, that is what the pairwise comparison is for.

lessons-learned.name: Lessons Learned
lessons-learned.whenToUse: When the experiences of a project are to be recorded — what went well, what did not, the root cause and the recommendation with its actions; not for day-to-day task tracking and not for a root-cause analysis itself, which is what the task list and the 5-Why analysis are for.

makigami.name: Makigami Matrix
makigami.description: Swim-lane process analysis with processing/waiting times and waste classification
makigami.whenToUse: When a cross-department process is to be recorded step by step with responsibility, processing time, waiting time and waste categories so that idle time becomes visible; not for the flow logic itself with its decisions and branches, which is what a flowchart is for.

model-data-generator.name: Model Data Generator
model-data-generator.description: Generate synthetic datasets from configurable regression models
model-data-generator.whenToUse: When synthetic data from a known regression model is needed — to practise DOE analysis and regression, or to test methods against a known “true” model — with factors, coefficients, noise and a seed for reproducible results.

morphological-box.name: Morphological Box
morphological-box.description: Combine solution concepts from parameters and options, check incompatibilities
morphological-box.whenToUse: When a solution consists of several sub-functions and alternative whole concepts should be combined systematically — not for scoring or choosing the concepts, that belongs to solution selection.

mosaic.name: Mosaic Plot
mosaic.description: Visualises the joint distribution of two categorical variables — column widths show the marginal frequency, segment heights show the conditional shares.
mosaic.whenToUse: Compare how two categorical variables combine: column widths show the share of each x category, segment heights the share of each group within it.

msa-typ1.name: MSA Type 1 (Cg/Cgk)
msa-typ1.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 1 — Repeatability (Cg) and Bias (Cgk)
msa-typ1.whenToUse: When the capability of a single gage should be checked: a standard or reference part is measured repeatedly, giving repeatability (Cg) and bias (Cgk) — not for measurement systems with several appraisers or parts, which the type 2, 4, 5 and 6 studies cover. Requires the measurements as a numeric column of a data collection.

msa-typ2.name: MSA Type 2/3 (Gage R&R)
msa-typ2.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 2 (with operator, Gage R&R) and Type 3 (no operator, automated measurement systems)
msa-typ2.whenToUse: When a measurement system with several parts (and usually several appraisers) should be assessed: a crossed study gives repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) by ANOVA; without an operator column the module computes as type 3 for automated measurement systems — not for the capability of a single gage on a standard, which type 1 covers. Requires parts, optionally appraisers, and the measurements as columns of a data collection.

msa-typ4.name: MSA Type 4 (linearity)
msa-typ4.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 4 — linearity and bias across the measurement range (AIAG %Lin, VDA 5 Q_MS,BI)
msa-typ4.whenToUse: When you need to check whether a measurement system measures equally correctly across the whole range: reference values and measured values as columns give the bias per reference point and a regression of the bias over the range (AIAG %linearity or VDA 5 Q_MS,BI) — not for capability on a single standard, which type 1 covers. Requires a reference column and a measured column of a data collection.

msa-typ5.name: MSA Type 5 (attribute)
msa-typ5.description: Attribute Measurement System Analysis — multiple appraisers, kappa-based agreement (Cohen, Fleiss, weighted)
msa-typ5.whenToUse: When an attribute measurement system (good/bad, classes, ordinal levels) is to be assessed: several appraisers rate parts, repeatedly, against an optional reference. The result is kappa agreement, effectiveness and a verdict by AIAG or Bosch rules — not for measured characteristics, which types 1 to 3 cover. Requires a data collection with a part column and either an appraiser and a rating column (long layout) or one rating column per appraiser and trial (wide layout).

msa-typ6.name: MSA Type 6 (stability)
msa-typ6.description: Stability / long-term behavior — control chart (I-MR/x̄-R) over a repeatedly measured reference part, Nelson rules 1–8 and a linear drift test
msa-typ6.whenToUse: When a measurement system has to stay stable over time: a reference part is measured repeatedly, the control chart (I-MR or x̄-R) shows violations of the Nelson rules, and a linear drift test checks for a trend. Needs a data collection with a value column, optionally a timestamp column and, for x̄-R, a subgroup column — not for the spread of a single measurement series, use types 1 to 3 for that.

multi-vari.name: Multi-Vari Chart
multi-vari.description: Stages single measurements across up to four factors and splits the spread into variance components — shows where the variation actually comes from.
multi-vari.whenToUse: When the spread of a measured characteristic must be traced to its sources: stages every single measurement by two to four factors (for example shift, cavity, part) and splits the variance into components, nested or crossed, by ANOVA or REML; needs one numeric measurement column and two factor columns.

multivariate-control-chart.name: Multivariate Control Chart (Hotelling T²)
multivariate-control-chart.whenToUse: Monitor several correlated characteristics together: Hotelling T² flags rows whose combination is unusual even when each value alone is in control.

opportunity-flowchart.name: Opportunity Flowchart
opportunity-flowchart.description: Two-column flow: value-added steps versus rework
opportunity-flowchart.whenToUse: When an existing chain needs sorting into value-added work versus rework — not for capturing a new process without that distinction yet.

outlier-test.name: Outlier Test
outlier-test.description: Run classical outlier tests (Grubbs, Dixon Q, Generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-Score) in parallel on a column
outlier-test.whenToUse: When a measured characteristic may contain outliers: tests one numeric column with up to seven methods (Grubbs, Dixon Q, generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-score, modified Z-score) and reports which values each method flags; requires at least 3 numeric values.

pairwise-comparison.name: Pairwise Comparison
pairwise-comparison.description: Prioritize criteria through systematic pairwise comparison. Every criterion is judged against every other.
pairwise-comparison.whenToUse: When a handful of equally ranked criteria needs a justified order and handing out points directly would be too arbitrary — every criterion is put against every other one, three to fifteen criteria; not when the criteria are to be weighted against SEVERAL outputs, which is what the C&E matrix is for.

pareto.name: Pareto Chart
pareto.description: Bar chart sorted by descending value with a cumulative-percentage line — the classic "vital few" tool.
pareto.whenToUse: Rank categories by frequency or by a summed value to find the vital few — with a cumulative percentage line.

pie-chart.name: Pie Chart
pie-chart.whenToUse: Show how a total splits into parts: one slice per distinct value, or per label with the values summed.

probability-plot.name: Probability Plot
probability-plot.description: Normal probability plot for checking normality, with optional grouping
probability-plot.whenToUse: Check whether one or more numeric columns follow a distribution: points on the straight line mean a good fit.

process-capability.name: Process Capability
process-capability.description: Process Capability Analysis — Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk, PPM, Sigma Level
process-capability.whenToUse: When it must be shown how well a process keeps a measured characteristic inside its specification limits: Cp and Cpk (short term, from the within-subgroup spread), Pp and Ppk (long term), PPM and sigma level, with confidence intervals. Works with one-sided or two-sided limits, individual values or subgroups. Needs at least one limit (lower or upper) and at least 2 numeric values from a data collection column or from loaded example data.

project-charter.name: Project Charter
project-charter.description: Project mandate: problem statement and measurable goals
project-charter.whenToUse: At the start of a project, to record the problem, measurable goals and the project organisation — the basis every later phase refers to.

raci-matrix.name: RACI Matrix
raci-matrix.description: Responsibility Assignment Matrix: roles per activity and stakeholder
raci-matrix.whenToUse: When each activity of an undertaking needs a record of who does the work (R), who is accountable (A), who is consulted (C) and who is informed (I) — the check reports every row without an R, without an A or with more than one A; not for describing the flow itself, which is what a flowchart is for.

random-generator.name: Random Generator
random-generator.description: Generate reproducible samples from statistical distributions
random-generator.whenToUse: When random data from a known distribution or from weighted categories is needed — for practice, simulations or test data — reproducible through the seed.

rare-event-chart.name: Control Chart (Rare Events)
rare-event-chart.description: g and t charts for rare events
rare-event-chart.whenToUse: Monitor rare events: the g chart counts opportunities between events, the t chart the time between events.

resampling.name: Resampling
resampling.description: Bootstrap confidence intervals and permutation tests for one, two, paired and k samples
resampling.whenToUse: When a statistic of one, two, paired or k samples needs a confidence interval or a test without assuming a distribution: bootstraps the interval (BCa or percentile) and tests by permutation (two samples, paired, k groups) or against a target value (one sample). Each sample needs at least 2 numeric values (10 for Ppk).

run-chart.name: Run Chart
run-chart.description: Median run chart with four runs tests
run-chart.whenToUse: Look at a series over time for non-random patterns — clustering, mixtures, trends, oscillation — before building control limits.

sample-size.name: Sample Size
sample-size.description: Calculate the required sample size for variance and mean tests
sample-size.whenToUse: When you need to know how many observations a test requires: computes the required sample size for variance tests (chi-square, F) and mean tests (one- and two-sample t) from the effect to detect, the significance level and the target power.

short-run-chart.name: Control Chart (Short-Run Z-MR)
short-run-chart.description: Standardised I-MR across parts with different targets
short-run-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart short production runs that mix parts with different targets: each value is standardised within its part and plotted on one Z-MR chart.

sipoc.name: SIPOC
sipoc.whenToUse: When the boundaries of a process need clarifying — who supplies, what goes in, which steps run, what comes out and who receives it; not for the flow itself with its decisions and branches, which is what a flowchart is for.

stakeholder-analysis.name: Stakeholder Analysis
stakeholder-analysis.description: Identify, assess, and plan communication with project stakeholders
stakeholder-analysis.whenToUse: When the stakeholders of a project need recording and placing by power and interest so that communication can follow that order; not for assigning responsibility to activities, which is what the RACI matrix is for.

survey-builder.name: Survey builder
survey-builder.description: Create VoC questionnaires, send them as HTML, import and evaluate the answers
survey-builder.whenToUse: When customers or stakeholders are to be surveyed in writing: design the questionnaire, send it as an HTML file per recipient, read in the answer files and evaluate them — without a server, the data stays in the project.

time-weighted-chart.name: Control Chart (Time-Weighted)
time-weighted-chart.description: EWMA and CUSUM for small persistent shifts
time-weighted-chart.whenToUse: Detect small, persistent shifts earlier than a Shewhart chart: EWMA weights recent values, CUSUM accumulates deviations from the target.

todo.name: Todo
todo.description: Task list with status, due date, and owner
todo.whenToUse: When the open tasks of a project need tracking with an owner, a due date and a status — not for scheduling in a calendar view and not for rating or selecting measures, which is what the calendar module and the rating matrices are for.

transformed-imr-chart.name: Control Chart (Box-Cox transformed)
transformed-imr-chart.description: I-MR with Box-Cox transform for non-normal data
transformed-imr-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart skewed, strictly positive data: a Box-Cox transformation makes them near-normal before I-MR limits are computed.

triz-9-windows.name: 9 Windows (TRIZ System Operator)
triz-9-windows.description: Examine the system on time × hierarchy axes
triz-9-windows.whenToUse: When a problem is to be looked at in its context — three system levels by three time windows — to find causes and solution spaces outside the system itself; not to follow a single chain of causes, which is what 5-why or Ishikawa are for.

triz-contradiction-matrix.name: Contradiction Matrix (TRIZ)
triz-contradiction-matrix.whenToUse: When two different engineering parameters are in conflict — improving one degrades the other — and the matrix should name the proven solution principles for that pair; not when a single parameter itself would have to hold two opposite values, which is what the physical contradiction is for.

triz-evolution-trends.name: Trends of Technical Evolution (TRIZ)
triz-evolution-trends.description: Eight classical evolution trajectories — locate the system and identify the next stage jump
triz-evolution-trends.whenToUse: When the question is where a system sits on the classical evolution trajectories and which stage jump comes next — not to resolve a specific contradiction or pick a variant.

triz-function-analysis.name: Function Analysis (TRIZ)
triz-function-analysis.description: Components, interactions and function model – the starting point for the other TRIZ tools
triz-function-analysis.whenToUse: When a technical system is to be broken down component by component to find harmful, insufficient and excessive functions and to spot trimming candidates by value and cost — not for a contradiction that is already named; the contradiction matrix and the physical contradiction cover that.

triz-ifr.name: Ideal Final Result (TRIZ)
triz-ifr.description: State the ideal and work backwards to a solution
triz-ifr.whenToUse: When a target image is needed to work backwards from towards a solution — not to judge a solution already found or to pick between variants.

triz-physical-contradiction.name: Physical Contradiction (TRIZ)
triz-physical-contradiction.description: One parameter must be A and ¬A — resolution via four separation principles
triz-physical-contradiction.whenToUse: When a single parameter would have to hold two opposite values at the same time and the contradiction is to be resolved by separation in time, space, condition or system level — not for a contradiction between two different characteristics, which is what the contradiction matrix is for.

triz-resources.name: Resources Checklist (TRIZ)
triz-resources.description: Systematic inventory of substances, fields, space, time, information and functions
triz-resources.whenToUse: When you want to inventory what the system and its environment already provide at no cost, before searching for solutions — not to judge solutions or resolve contradictions.

triz-sufield.name: Substance-Field Analysis (TRIZ)
triz-sufield.description: Model the interaction as an S1-S2-field triangle and apply Altshuller's 76 standard solutions
triz-sufield.whenToUse: When an action between two substances is too weak, too strong, harmful or missing altogether and the matching TRIZ standard solutions are to be found; not to resolve a contradiction between two parameters — that is what the contradiction matrix is for.

unit-converter.name: Unit Converter
unit-converter.whenToUse: When a measured value has to be expressed in another unit — length, area, volume, mass, pressure, temperature, force, torque, energy, power, flow rate, speed, time, angle, rotational speed, pH, concentration, sound or lab values — or when a time has to be converted between two time zones; not for converting a whole data column, that is what the data transformation is for.

voc-ctx-tree.name: VoC → CTx Tree
voc-ctx-tree.description: Translate Voice of Customer into measurable CTx requirements
voc-ctx-tree.whenToUse: When customer statements should be translated into a chain of requirements — the voice of the customer, the need behind it, the measurable driver (CTQ, CTD, CTC) and the testable requirement with a target value and a measure; not for collecting or rating customer statements themselves, that is what the survey and Kano tools are for.

worksheet.name: Data Collection
worksheet.description: Spreadsheet for data entry and management
worksheet.whenToUse: The shared data substrate: measurements land here before an analysing tool reads them through a column reference. Almost every analysis starts with a data collection.

xy-plot.name: XY Plot
xy-plot.description: Create scatter plots from worksheet columns
xy-plot.whenToUse: Show the relationship between two numeric columns as a scatter plot, optionally grouped or as bubbles sized by a third column.
